anomalies.observed: The drawing shows only one 0 Ω serial-mode jumper, R20, tying one servo-signal node to NET0030. The second servo-signal node, on the right side of the 1 kΩ resistor R14 and connected to J5, is tied to NET0030 by a plain wire rather than by a selectable 0 Ω jumper.
anomalies.expected: The specification states that R13 and R14 are 0 Ω jumpers used only for serial-servo mode: “When shorted, bridge J3-pin3 and J8-pin3 together and onto the MAX3485 TTL bus,” and the schematic annotation says “Short R13, R14 for Serial Servo.” In PWM mode these jumpers should be open so the servo signal lines are isolated from the MAX3485 bus.

evidence.quote: Right side of U2/servo section: “R20 0” is present, while “R14 1k” feeds the J5 signal node and that node is connected to the “NET0030” label without a second 0 Ω jumper; annotation: “Short R13, R14 for Serial Servo”
R13, R14 | 0 Ω (jumpers) | When shorted, bridge J3-pin3 and J8-pin3 together and onto the MAX3485 TTL bus

anomalies.impact: The PWM/serial mode selection is not implemented as specified: one servo signal is permanently connected to the MAX3485 bus. In PWM mode this loads/fights the second PWM servo signal through the MAX3485 bias/receiver network, and the intended jumper-selectable isolation of PortC is lost.

parsed.summary: The schematic appears to omit the second serial-mode 0 Ω jumper and instead hard-wires one servo signal to NET0030, violating the specified jumper-selectable PWM/serial servo interface.
